testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When a tire goes flat, you may hear a loud bang. When will the truck be affected?

options.text: Only if the flat tire is at the front.
Only if the truck is carrying cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: A few seconds later.
questions.explanation: There is usually a delay of a few seconds between hearing the tire fail and feeling the truck respond. Because of this delay, you might think the sound came from another vehicle.

questions.question: If you are turning left and there are two left turn lanes, which one should you use?

options.text: Large trucks should not turn at intersections with two left turn lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need extra space to turn left. When there are two left turn lanes, use the right lane so you have room to swing right before turning.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Move quickly before other vehicles can block you.
Move slowly in case another vehicle is in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move slowly in case another vehicle is in the lane.
questions.explanation: Always change lanes slowly and smoothly. If there is a vehicle you did not see, the driver will have more time to react to you.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, what should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.
Respond to the driver's rude gestures.
Challenge the driver to a race.
Ignore the driver if you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ignore the driver if you can.
questions.explanation: If you meet an aggressive driver, get away from them if possible. Do not make eye contact, challenge them, or respond to rude gestures. This will keep you safe.

questions.question: What is a header board used for?

options.text: To help the driver see behind them.
To protect the driver from cargo that moves.
To prevent the driver from leaving the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: To protect the driver from cargo that moves.
questions.explanation: Header boards (also called "headache racks") protect the driver if cargo shifts during a crash or hard stop.

questions.question: What happens if a cargo cover flaps while you are driving?

options.text: It helps keep the cargo cool.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can tear off.
questions.explanation: A cargo cover should not flap in the wind while driving. It could tear loose and uncover the cargo, blocking your view or the view of other drivers.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, the landing gear should be:

options.text: More worn on the passenger side than the driver side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fully raised.
questions.explanation: Check that the landing gear has all its parts, is fully raised, the crank handle is secure, and the support frame is not damaged.

questions.question: What do air tank drains do?

options.text: Allow rain water to enter the tanks.
Remove water and oil from the air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains water and compressor oil. These build up in the tanks and can damage the brakes. You must open the manual air tank drains daily to remove this buildup.

questions.question: After cargo is secured, how often should you check it?

options.text: You do not need to check it again during the trip.
You can drive eight hours without checking it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every three hours or 150 miles.
questions.explanation: Check cargo before starting, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles.

questions.question: When carrying a wide load, what should you do?

options.text: Get special permits and follow special rules.
Honk at other drivers to move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get special permits and follow special rules.
questions.explanation: Loads that are too long, too wide, or too heavy may need special permits. These loads have restrictions, such as driving only at certain times.

questions.question: In very hot weather, tires should be checked regularly because:

options.text: Air pressure may increase as the temperature rises.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure may increase as the temperature rises.
questions.explanation: Hot air expands, so tire pressure can become dangerously high in very hot weather. If this happens, stop and let your tires cool down. Do not release air, as the pressure will drop too much when the tires cool.

questions.question: A tank endorsement is:

options.text: Required to transport both liquids and gases.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required to transport both liquids and gases.
questions.explanation: You need a tank endorsement to drive a tank vehicle that carries liquids or gases.

questions.question: When driving down a steep grade:

options.text: You should ride your brakes all the way down.
Shift into a higher gear to slow down your vehicle.
Shift into lower gears to slow down your vehicle.
Put the truck in neutral to slow down your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift into lower gears to slow down your vehicle.
questions.explanation: When going down a steep hill, use the engine's braking power to slow down. Use your brakes only to supplement this method and prevent overheating.

questions.question: Roads are most slippery right after it begins to rain because:

options.text: The water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
The gravel gets washed to the middle of the lane.
Some tires are not designed for rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: The water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, water mixes with oil that has dripped onto the road, creating a slippery surface.

questions.question: What does driving intrastate mean?

options.text: Traveling from one state to another state

questions.correctAnswerText: Traveling within a single state
questions.explanation: Intrastate driving means you drive a commercial vehicle only within one state, and your cargo does not leave that state.

questions.question: How much water must be on a road surface for a vehicle to hydroplane?

options.text: A good amount, such as a large puddle

questions.correctAnswerText: A small amount
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when tires lose grip and slide on water. Only a small amount of water on the road is needed for this to occur.

questions.question: While driving a vehicle, if an unusual noise or feeling occurs, the driver should:

options.text: Assume it is not a concern and continue driving.
Hope the vehicle makes it until another driver takes over.
Stop and check the vehicle to find the problem.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and check the vehicle to find the problem.
questions.explanation: If you notice, hear, smell, or feel anything unusual while driving, stop immediately and inspect the vehicle.

questions.question: When using a fire extinguisher on a fire, you should:

options.text: Get as close to the fire as possible.
Stay as far away from the fire as possible.
Aim the extinguisher at the top of the flames.
Aim the fire extinguisher at the ground about two feet away from the fire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay as far away from the fire as possible.
questions.explanation: Keep your distance from the fire. Aim the extinguisher at the base of the flames, not the top.

questions.question: Tread depth in the major grooves on a front tire should be at least:
questions.correctAnswerText: 4/32 of an inch.
questions.explanation: Front tires must have at least 4/32 of an inch of tread depth in every major groove. Other tires must have at least 2/32 of an inch.

questions.question: Driving at night is:

options.text: Safer than driving during the day.
Just as safe as driving during the day.
More dangerous than driving during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous than driving during the day.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous. It is harder to see hazards, headlights can cause glare, and more tired and impaired drivers are on the road.

questions.question: What is the name of a thin layer of ice that forms on road surfaces?
questions.correctAnswerText: Black ice
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice on the road. You can see the road surface through it. A road with black ice looks wet. Be very careful when temperatures are below freezing and the road looks wet.

questions.question: What will you be asked to do during the vehicle inspection test?

options.text: Explain what you would inspect and why
Estimate the weight of a load in a trailer

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you would inspect and why
questions.explanation: During the CDL vehicle inspection test, you must inspect your vehicle. You will tell the examiner what you are inspecting and why.

questions.question: What can a trailer brake hand valve be used for?

options.text: Stop the vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop
questions.explanation: If a truck has a trailer brake hand valve, you can use it to stop the vehicle from rolling backward when you start from a stop.

questions.question: When driving in wet conditions, what does it mean if other vehicles are not spraying water?

options.text: Ice has formed on the road
The spray is caught under the vehicle
The tires have soaked up all the moisture

questions.correctAnswerText: Ice has formed on the road
questions.explanation: If the road looks wet but other vehicles' wheels are not spraying water, ice has formed on the road. Drive with extra care on wet or icy roads.

questions.question: When should you shift into a lower gear to drive down a hill?

options.text: As you go downhill and pick up speed
Near the bottom of the hill

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start moving downhill
questions.explanation: Always downshift before you start driving downhill. Shifting to a lower gear at high speed can damage the transmission and reduce your engine braking power. Choose a safe speed based on how steep the hill is, how long it is, your vehicle's weight, road conditions, and weather.

questions.question: How many red reflective warning triangles should drivers use when their vehicle is stopped on the road?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three
questions.explanation: Place three red reflective warning triangles on the road when your vehicle is stopped.

questions.question: What can change a vehicle's height?
questions.correctAnswerText: Weight
questions.explanation: A heavy load makes a vehicle sit lower. A light load makes a vehicle sit higher. A vehicle that fits under a bridge when fully loaded may not fit when empty.

questions.question: A load that is 40 feet long needs a minimum of how many tie-downs?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. You must use at least two tie-downs, no matter what size the cargo is.

questions.question: What might a vehicle stopped at a green light indicate about the driver?

options.text: The driver does not know the rules of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver is impaired
questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs of impaired driving. Drivers who have drunk alcohol, are tired, are on drugs, or are sick can be dangerous. One sign of impaired driving is stopping at inappropriate places, like green traffic lights.

questions.question: What should be done with wheel rims that have been welded?

options.text: Place them in the front of the vehicle
Place them in the rear of the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use them
questions.explanation: Do not use wheels or rims that have been welded. They are not safe. Replace any damaged wheels and rims.

questions.question: When should service brakes be tested?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every trip.
questions.explanation: Always test your service brakes before you drive. This helps you find any problems before you need to brake while driving.

questions.question: What is aggressive driving?

options.text: Driving in a selfish or pushy way without caring about others
Driving with some care for other drivers' safety

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving in a selfish or pushy way without caring about others
questions.explanation: Aggressive driving means operating your vehicle in a selfish, bold, or pushy way without regard for others' rights or safety.

questions.question: What must you do if your load is too long?

options.text: Place a warning flag at the end of the load.
Transport it only between 6 p.m. and 3 a.m.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place a warning flag at the end of the load.
questions.explanation: When carrying a load that is too long, you must use warning flags or flashing lights. You will also need permits. Driving times may be limited to certain hours.

questions.question: How often must you check that cargo is secure?
questions.correctAnswerText: Every 150 miles
questions.explanation: Check that cargo is secure before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles.

questions.question: What should you do if your brake pedal loses pressure?

options.text: Hold the brake pedal down as far as possible

questions.correctAnswerText: Downshift
questions.explanation: If your brakes lose pressure, shift to a lower gear. This will help slow your vehicle.

questions.question: When inspecting the steering box, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Check that the steering box is securely mounted
Check for power steering fluid leaks
Assume all cotter keys are present

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume all cotter keys are present
questions.explanation: Before a trip, make sure the steering box is securely mounted. Check for missing nuts, bolts, and cotter keys. Look for power steering fluid leaks and damage to hoses.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a cargo lift, what should you check?

options.text: That the lift is loosely attached
That the lift is not leaking
That the lift is fully extended
That the lift is the correct color

questions.correctAnswerText: That the lift is not leaking
questions.explanation: When checking a cargo lift, look for leaks, damage, or missing parts. The lift must be fully closed and locked securely.

questions.question: How many side mirrors should a registered vehicle have?

options.text: One mirror on the left side only
Mirrors on both the left and right sides
One mirror on the right side only

questions.correctAnswerText: Mirrors on both the left and right sides
questions.explanation: Your vehicle needs mirrors on both sides so you can see what is happening around your vehicle. Check these mirrors regularly while driving.

questions.question: When exiting a bus during the skills test, what must you do?

options.text: Keep both hands on the handrail

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handrail firmly
questions.explanation: When exiting a bus during the skills test, face the vehicle and always maintain three points of contact. Hold the handrail firmly. Exiting incorrectly may result in automatic failure.

questions.question: What air pressure must build up before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes?
questions.correctAnswerText: 100 psi
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, let the air compressor build up at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: When you stop on the side of a highway, how far behind your vehicle should you place warning devices?
questions.correctAnswerText: 10, 100, and 200 feet
questions.explanation: Place warning devices 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet behind your vehicle when you stop on the side of a highway.

questions.question: When you approach your vehicle, you should check for:

options.text: Whether the vehicle is shiner than other vehicles.
Whether the vehicle is parked too close to other vehicles.
Puddles under the vehicle that show a leak.
Whether the vehicle is parked properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Puddles under the vehicle that show a leak.
questions.explanation: When you approach your vehicle, look under it for fresh leaks. Also check around the vehicle for hazards like people, other vehicles, or low-hanging wires or tree limbs.

questions.question: What is a tire load?

options.text: The minimum safe weight a tire can carry
The maximum safe weight a tire can carry
The weight of the air in a fully inflated tire

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe weight a tire can carry
questions.explanation: Tire load is the maximum weight a tire can safely carry at a specified pressure. You will find this information on the side of the tire.

questions.question: When must you sign a written vehicle inspection report?

options.text: Only if defects were found and repaired or confirmed as not needing repair.
Only if repairs cost more than $1,000.
Only if a law enforcement officer asks you to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if defects were found and repaired or confirmed as not needing repair.
questions.explanation: You must sign the previous vehicle inspection report only if defects were noted and certified to have been repaired or confirmed as not needing repair.

questions.question: When driving in fog and you see lights ahead, what should you know?

options.text: The lights are on the road.
The lights may be a reflection.
The lights may be an optical illusion.
The lights may not show where the road is because the vehicle may have left the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lights may not show where the road is because the vehicle may have left the road.
questions.explanation: In fog, lights are not a reliable guide to where the road is. A vehicle with lights may have pulled off the road.

questions.question: What are placards?

options.text: Signs on a vehicle that identify hazardous cargo
A type of tire used in snowy conditions

questions.correctAnswerText: Signs on a vehicle that identify hazardous cargo
questions.explanation: Placards are diamond-shaped warning signs placed on the outside of vehicles carrying hazardous materials. They identify the specific hazard classes of the cargo.

questions.question: After you stop during a stop and start maneuver, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the vehicle in first gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the parking brake.
questions.explanation: When you park during the stop and start maneuver on the driving skills test, apply the parking brake. Shift into neutral or park. Park parallel to the curb and do not block driveways or intersections.

questions.question: When using mirrors while driving, you should:

options.text: Look in the mirrors for a long time.
Use only the driver's side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look in the mirrors quickly.
questions.explanation: Staring at the mirrors for too long is dangerous. You will travel a long distance without looking at the road ahead.

questions.question: How should you do pre-trip inspections?

options.text: Differently each time, focusing on different items.
The same way each time to avoid forgetting something.
Have someone other than the driver do it.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way each time to avoid forgetting something.
questions.explanation: Do pre-trip inspections the same way every time. This helps you remember all the important steps and keeps you from forgetting anything.

questions.question: During the skills test, when making a turn that requires a stop, what should you do?

options.text: Stop after the stop line to see better.
Keep the front wheels aimed straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the front wheels aimed straight ahead.
questions.explanation: When you must stop before making a turn on the driving skills test, come to a smooth stop behind the stop line, crosswalk, or sign. Keep your front wheels aimed straight ahead and do not let your vehicle roll. If there is a vehicle ahead, stop where you can still see its rear tires.
